findings.title: Store-load boundary passes NaN: a "NaN" leaf reaches the live model and makes the next save undecodable
findings.claim: store._poisoned returns False for float('nan') and for the string "NaN" (abs(nan) >= ABSURD is False), so QuarantiningStore.async_load hands those leaves to the loaders; in 3 of 515 single-leaf "NaN" substitutions over every d1-stores healthy payload the NaN reaches the live thermal model or the published payload, and in the same 3 the next save writes a bare NaN token that the following restart's orjson load refuses, dropping the whole accuracy and snapshots documents.
findings.mechanism: _poisoned's float branch is `abs(value) >= ABSURD`; NaN compares False, so _sanitize keeps it although the module and _poisoned's own docstring say non-finite is quarantined. comfort_learning's from_dict reads `float(np.clip(float('NaN'), lo, hi))` = nan (np.clip propagates NaN) into learned_weight/evidence, published as data['comfort_learning']; DhwProfileLearner.apply_cooling_rate does the same into ThermalParameters.dhw_cooling_rate (the solver's input). The accuracy and snapshot savers then json.dumps the NaN as a bare token; Home Assistant's orjson load refuses it and moves the whole file aside, so the learned accuracy history and the snapshots are lost at the next restart. tests/finite_boundary.py's own module-level checks 'the boundary quarantines nan at every depth' and 'str-nan' print FAIL on this tree.

evidence.unit: leaves (of 515) whose NaN reaches the live model/published payload; same 3 make a stored document undecodable
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: other finder seats and this seat's fuzz shards running; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --fix: store._poisoned also returns True for a non-finite float or a string whose float() is non-finite (one line: `return not math.isfinite(value) or abs(value) >= ABSURD`), patched in memory

findings.metric_definition: Count of single numeric leaves which, set to the string "NaN" and loaded through the real loaders plus one cycle, leave a non-finite value live/published or an undecodable store document.
findings.phenomenon_property: No store load hands a loader a non-finite number in any spelling (float NaN/inf, or a string float() turns into one); every non-finite leaf is quarantined at QuarantiningStore.async_load, so nothing non-finite is installed live or re-saved.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D1/s2/nan_boundary.py  (every numeric leaf of every d1-stores payload; the seam is store._poisoned, one function)

findings.proposed_fix_scope: store.py:_poisoned refuses non-finite floats (math.isfinite); add a NaN arm to tests/finite_boundary.py's run (its own module-level check already fails).

findings.title: PV production is read with no age check: a silent or future-stamped meter still seeds step 0 and is published
findings.claim: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._pv_measured_production reads CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY through hass.states.get + state_power_kw, never through InputReader, so the 30-minute limit const.INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY] declares is never applied: in 6 of 6 report ages past the limit (31 min to 24 h) and for a report stamped 90 min in the future, the real cycle publishes data['pv']['measured_production_kw']=5.0 and overwrites step 0 of the PV forecast with it.
findings.mechanism: _pv_forecast sets production[0] = min(self._pv_production, peak_kw) from _pv_measured_production, which is `state_power_kw(self.hass.states.get(entity_id), sign='clamp')`. state_power_kw's own docstring calls itself 'the one parse of a power state outside InputReader (which adds the staleness of a configured input)'; the slot has a declared limit (const.py: INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY] = 30.0, INPUT_ON_CHANGE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES pv_production_entity 30.0) that no reader of it applies, and the slot never appears in the input watchdog (staleness.py: 'unread'). An inverter whose integration drops off mid-afternoon keeps the planner believing in its last output (here 5 kW) for the current step indefinitely, and a host clock stepped back makes the same reading look fresh.

evidence.unit: report ages past the 30-min limit (of 6) at which the stale reading is published and used; plus future_published=1
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count

perturbation.change: --fix: _pv_measured_production first reads the slot through InputReader(hass, {}).read(CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY, entity_id=...) and returns None unless the reading is ok (the declared age limit applies), then state_power_kw as before; patched in memory
perturbation.observed_value: stale_cells_published=0, future_published=0; ages 5 and 20 min still publish 5.0

findings.metric_definition: Of 6 report ages beyond INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[pv_production] (31,45,90,180,420,1440 min), how many cycles still publish pv.measured_production_kw from the stale state.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every configured input with a declared age limit is read under that limit by every consumer; a reading past its limit (or stamped ahead of the clock) is not used as a measurement and not published as one.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D1/s2/consumers.py  (per d1-inputs slot, the production functions calling hass.states.get on it; a slot listed in const.INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES whose getters bypass InputReader/age_of is a seam)

findings.title: A weather forecast that stopped advancing is read as a recovery: published fresh while every row lies in the past
findings.claim: _fetch_weather treats any non-empty plausible get_forecasts reply as a successful fetch (_weather_fetch_recovered clears _weather_stale_since) without checking that its rows reach now, so in 5 of 5 cells where the provider keeps returning the same 48 rows and the clock is 1 to 48 h past the last row, the real cycle publishes weather_forecast_stale_hours=None (fresh) while the plan's outdoor array is the last row's 0.7 C held flat (the live weather entity says -3.0 C).
findings.mechanism: coordinator._plausible_forecast_rows filters non-dict rows and out-of-window field values only; a stale-but-well-formed forecast passes, `if forecast_data:` takes the success branch and calls _weather_fetch_recovered, which sets _weather_stale_since=None. _forecast_arrays then extrapolates the last row across the horizon. The empty-forecast and exception branches do mark the data stale (price_weather.py: weather_empty_hidden=0), so the staleness signal exists and only this branch skips it. A weather integration that stops refreshing its forecast (a cached provider, an expired API key that keeps serving the last answer) leaves the plan on a days-old trajectory while the published freshness says nothing is wrong.

evidence.unit: cells (of 5) with every forecast row in the past published as fresh (stale_hours None)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count

perturbation.change: --fix: coordinator._plausible_forecast_rows also drops a row whose hour (datetime + 1 h) has ended, patched in memory, so an all-past reply is an empty one and takes the existing stale branch

findings.metric_definition: Of 5 cells 1/6/12/24/48 h past the last row of a non-advancing forecast, cycles publishing weather_forecast_stale_hours None.
findings.phenomenon_property: A feed reply that does not cover now is not a fresh fetch: the forecast's staleness (weather_forecast_stale_hours) is set whenever the forecast the plan stands on no longer reaches the current step, whatever branch delivered it.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D1/s2/price_weather.py  (each external feed's success branch -- weather, Tibber, price entity -- driven with a reply that no longer covers now; the price feeds hold, weather does not)

findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py:_fetch_weather: a reply whose rows end before the current step is a failed fetch (_weather_fetch_failed), so stale_hours and the plan's stale marking apply.

findings.title: off_restore._armed_record marks loaded before its read lands: a concurrent caller sees no hold and saves that
findings.claim: off_restore._armed_record sets held.loaded = True before awaiting load_mapping and takes no lock, so a second caller while the first read is in flight gets an empty armed set: with the persisted record holding the heat curve's baseline (3.0) and async_armed_entry's read pending, async_restore (entering MODE_OFF, or unload) sends 0 restore writes instead of 1 and saves {"armed": {}}, which QuarantiningStore.async_save writes after the read lands -- so the hold is not released now and the baseline is gone from disk for the next restart (2 of 2 consequences; 0 when the two calls are serial).
findings.mechanism: QuarantiningStore.async_save waits for the read in flight, but _save(held) builds its payload from held.armed before calling it, so the store-level wait cannot help: the payload is the pre-read empty set. The sibling with the same 'loaded before the await' shape, pump_arbiter._load, is safe because both its callers (apply, the switch-on pass) hold held.lock; off_restore has no lock and five public entry points (async_arm, async_restore, async_armed_entry, async_rebaseline, async_consumer_state) reach _armed_record from the heat-curve publish, the pump arbiter, set_mode and unload, which run as separate loop tasks. The exposure is the first read of an entry's record after a start: a set_mode('off')/unload, or a second consumer, landing while the first cycle's heat-curve arm is reading.

evidence.unit: consequences of 2 (restore not sent; armed baseline missing from the saved document)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count (the read suspension is a fixed 10 ms sleep, the ordering is deterministic)

findings.phenomenon_property: No caller of a lazily loaded persisted record observes it before its read lands, and no save of that record can carry a payload built before the read: the first read is shared and awaited by every caller.

findings.title: One wrong-typed numeric option in an earlier-version config entry fails setup or every cycle, with no quarantine
findings.claim: async_migrate_entry only stamps the version, and ThermalParameters.from_config / _tabled_values / _flow_curve_values and comfort_band.effective read numeric options raw (no coercion, or a bare float()), so of 1200 seeded single-option mutants of a healthy all-features entry stamped v1..v6, 54 make the coordinator constructor raise (setup fails) and 88 make both cycles raise UpdateFailed (every update fails) -- 142 permanent failures, 21 to 26 per version -- with nothing logged as a quarantined option and no reset.
findings.mechanism: _tabled_values copies ~50 numeric options straight from the entry (`config.get(KEY, DEFAULT)`, no float()), with the comment 'Booleans are coerced because a config entry may carry a string' -- numbers are not; a string or null dhw_tank_volume then raises in dhw_tank_thermal_mass on every cycle ('can't multiply sequence by non-int of type float'). from_config's own float(config.get(CONF_MAX_TEMP ...)) and _flow_curve_values' float(config.get(CONF_TARGET_TEMP ...)) raise in the constructor on '', 'abc', None, a list or a dict; comfort_band.effective's float(candidate.get(...)) raises on every cycle for min_temperature. An entity slot holding a list/dict raises as an unhashable key in InputReader._begin on every cycle. Because the migration validates nothing, an entry written by an older release (or a hand-edited core.config_entries) with one such value never loads until the user edits the option.

evidence.unit: mutants (of 1200 over v1..v6) whose setup or every cycle fails
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, run as two shards beside this seat's other harnesses; a count

perturbation.change: --fix: async_migrate_entry additionally drops every option whose JSON type differs from the type the config flow writes for it (the healthy record's), so the reader falls back to its default; patched in memory

findings.title: A stored boosted_h past timedelta's range raises in the boost restore task on every restart
findings.claim: boost._restore_settle builds timedelta(hours=boosted_h) for any finite non-negative boosted_h, and store.ABSURD (1e15) admits values far past timedelta's range, so for 4 of 5 stored values (3e10, 1e11, 1e12, 1e14 h) the restore task the coordinator spawns raises OverflowError on both of two restarts (8 of 10), leaving the running space overlay's start (space_since) unrestored and the boosted time at timedelta(0) instead of the 'unknown' (None) the loader's own comment prescribes; the fifth (1e10 h) loads as ~47 000 years.
findings.mechanism: The guard `isinstance(hours, (int, float)) and 0.0 <= hours < math.inf` accepts any finite hours; held.space_settle_until is set before the timedelta call, so the raise leaves a half-applied restore and skips the space since/end handling below it; the exception escapes the spawned restore_session task (Home Assistant logs 'Task exception was never retrieved' each start). The document is not rewritten by the failed restore, so the same failure recurs at every restart until a later boost overwrites the store. DOMAINS declares the field `space_settle/boosted_h: _Z0`, which only the debug-level off-domain diagnostic reads.

evidence.unit: restarts (of 10: 5 values x 2 restarts on the same document) whose boost restore task raises
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count

findings.instrumented_symbol: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/boost.py:_restore_settle (via the coordinator constructor's spawn_restore_session -> restore_session -> restore, on a real loop; boost.held_for state read back)

perturbation.change: --fix: _restore_settle treats a boosted_h at or past timedelta.max in hours as unreadable (None), its docstring's rule for an unreadable value; patched in memory

findings.metric_definition: Restarts whose spawned boost restore task raises, over 5 out-of-range boosted_h values x 2 restarts on an unchanged document.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every stored duration a loader turns into a timedelta is bounded to what its writer can produce (or read as unknown) before conversion, so no stored number below store.ABSURD can raise out of a restore.
